transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well, it’s... it’s a lot, honestly. I work as a wholesale and retail buyer, and I’ve been doing this since I finished high school, so I know my job, I know how the inventory works, and I know how to spot when something is off. But lately, well, what really made me come in today is that I just... I can't shake this feeling that people at work are out to get me. And not just my coworkers, but even some of the outside vendors we deal with. 

It’s like they’re all secretly tracking my buys. I’ll put in the orders for a new product, I do all the math, I get everything set up perfectly, and then suddenly they are messing with the launch numbers. They’re altering the data just to make me look stupid. I mean, I spend hours on these accounts, and it’s like they have this coordinated effort to sabotage my performance and make it look like I don't know what I'm doing. 

I even went to my supervisor about it because I couldn't take it anymore. I laid it all out for him, but he just pulled up these system reports and tried to tell me that everything was normal. He spent like an hour showing me how the reports don't prove that anyone is messing with my numbers, but I just... I know what I see. I know they're tracking me. Even when he shows me that paperwork, it doesn't explain how the vendors know exactly when to shift the numbers to make my buys look like a total failure. It’s just constantly happening and I have to check everything three or four times because I know they are watching my system, and it’s just exhausting trying to do my job when everyone is messing with my work...
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

Well, it's... I mean, since you're asking, yeah. There is something else. I haven't told my supervisor this part because, you know, he already thinks I'm making up the data tracking stuff and I didn't want to give him an excuse to write me up. But sometimes... okay, so our main stockroom is this massive warehouse space, right? High ceilings, concrete floors, rows and rows of metal shelving. I'll be back there doing physical counts, and I always make sure I'm alone because I need to focus and make sure nobody is altering the physical inventory to match the fake numbers they put in the system. 

So I'm completely alone. But then, right out of nowhere, I'll hear this man's voice. It's so close, like... like he's standing literally right behind my shoulder. He tells me to move faster, Scott. Just like that, using my name. Or he'll just start laughing at my picks, like he thinks the products I'm choosing for the floor are a complete joke. I'll spin around immediately, ready to yell at whoever snuck up on me, ready to finally catch one of them in the act, but... there is never anybody there. Just empty aisles. The motion sensor lights don't even turn on in the next aisle over. 

And it's not just at work, either, which is the part that really messes with my head. I'll be driving back from a vendor meeting, totally alone in my own car, doors locked, just trying to process the meeting and figure out if the vendor was lying to me about the supply chain delays... and I'll hear that same man's voice from the backseat, just laughing at me or telling me I'm too slow. I pull over, I check the whole car, I look under the seats, and nobody is there. I just... I don't understand how someone is following me, or how he gets in my car without me seeing him, but I hear him as clearly as I'm hearing you right now. It's driving me crazy because I know I'm alone, but the voice is right there.
How long have these experiences been going on?

Well, let me think back... it’s been a while now. I mean, it didn't all just start overnight, you know? It’s been... gosh, roughly ten months now. Yeah, about ten months. 

I remember because it was right around the time we were gearing up for the third-quarter inventory push, which is always a nightmare anyway, but that’s when I first started noticing the discrepancies in the system. I thought maybe it was just a glitch at first, or maybe the vendors were just being sloppy with their data entry. But then it kept happening, week after week, and that’s when I realized it was deliberate. That they were actually tracking me. 

And the voice... the voice started around the same time, maybe a little bit after I first noticed the numbers being messed with. I remember the very first time I heard it, I was doing a spot check on a shipment of electronics that had just come in, and I was already stressed because the manifest didn't match the purchase order I had submitted. And then, right there in the receiving bay, I heard him. Just laughing at me. I spent twenty minutes looking behind every pallet, checking the loading dock, even asking the forklift driver if he had seen anyone walk past. But there was no one. 

So yeah, it’s been about ten months of this constant... this constant checking and re-checking, and looking over my shoulder, and trying to figure out how they’re doing it. Ten months of hearing that guy laugh at me in the warehouse, in my car, when I'm just trying to do my job. It’s exhausting, honestly. Ten whole months of feeling like I'm the only one who sees what's really going on, and having to deal with this voice on top of it all.
Have you had any periods during these ten months when the voices and the feeling that people are tracking you completely went away?

No, that's the thing... they never really stop. I mean, you'd think maybe if I just took a step back or got some rest it would go away, but it doesn't. There was this one stretch, I want to say it was maybe back in... April? Or early May? Right after the spring inventory reset, which is always a chaotic time. 

I actually had this period where things felt a lot calmer, at least as far as my physical energy went. Because for a while before that, I was just going and going, hardly sleeping at all, just feeling like I was an absolute genius. I literally felt like I was running the whole market, like I could predict every single consumer retail trend before it even happened and I was going to single-handedly double the company's profit margin. But then that kind of faded out, and I got back into a normal routine. I was actually sleeping through the night again, getting a solid seven or eight hours, eating regular meals, and just feeling a lot more level. I wasn't all revved up anymore.

But the crazy part is, even during that calmer stretch... even when I was sleeping normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market anymore, I still spent those few weeks completely believing that people were tracking my buys. I would sit at my desk, totally well-rested, feeling perfectly fine, and I still knew they were altering my spreadsheets. And the voice didn't stop either. I'd be back in the stockroom doing my pulls, feeling totally grounded, and that guy's voice would still be right there behind my shoulder, laughing at me. 

So no, it never completely goes away. Even when my energy was totally normal for those few weeks and everything else in my life seemed to settle down, the tracking and the voice were still happening exactly the same way. It just makes you realize how deep this whole sabotage thing really goes, because if it was just me being stressed out or overworked, wouldn't it have stopped when I was finally resting? But it didn't. It just kept happening.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was very high or irritable and you had much more energy than usual?

Yeah, that's exactly what I was talking about just a minute ago with the energy and feeling like a genius. I get these stretches where it goes on for a week, maybe two weeks, where I just have this insane amount of drive. It's like... it's honestly like the whole city is opening up for me. I’ll be driving downtown to check out a new supplier or heading to the warehouse, and I just feel this massive rush, like I hold the keys to the entire wholesale district and I can see exactly how every single piece of merchandise is going to move before it even hits the shelves. The energy is just vibrating right through me, and I feel like I can take on the entire world. 

But the thing is, it’s not always just a fun, productive feeling, because it makes me really... well, volatile, I guess. When I'm operating on that level, if someone gets in my way, it gets ugly fast. Like, if one of the higher-ups questions a purchase order I put together, or if my supervisor tells me I need to slow down and follow their standard pacing, I just completely lose it. I snap way harder than I mean to. 

I remember a few months back, a vendor was dragging his feet on a bulk invoice, just being totally incompetent, and he actually had the nerve to tell me I needed to calm down. I ended up just tearing into him over the phone, practically screaming about how he was bottlenecking my entire supply chain and how he couldn't see the big picture. It’s like all that incredible, high-flying energy just instantly sours into this furious irritation if anyone tries to pump the brakes on me. I'll pace around the stockroom just fuming, muttering to myself about how stupid everyone is. So, yeah, I definitely have those weeks. It's like I'm completely unstoppable, but everybody else is just moving in slow motion and it drives me absolutely insane when they try to drag me down to their speed.
Have the voices and feeling that people are tracking you ever happened when your mood was completely normal for at least two weeks?

Yeah, I mean... I know I brought this up a minute ago, but yes, definitely. It was... well, like I said, I think it was back in April, or maybe early May? Right after the big spring reset. I remember it specifically because that's usually when I crash anyway, just from the sheer volume of purchase orders I have to process. 

But yeah, I had this stretch—it was definitely at least two weeks, maybe even three—where I wasn't feeling like a genius anymore. I wasn't revved up, I wasn't snapping at the vendors, and I wasn't feeling like I held the keys to the city. I was just... normal. I was going to bed at a reasonable hour, actually sleeping through the night instead of pacing around my apartment trying to predict market trends. I was eating lunch, taking my breaks, just doing my job like a regular person. My mood was totally fine, completely level. 

But the crazy part—and this is what really gets me, this is what proves to me that it’s not just stress—is that even during that totally calm, normal stretch, I still knew they were tracking my buys. I would be sitting there at my desk, totally rested, feeling completely fine, and I would look at the spreadsheets and just know that someone had been in there altering the numbers. I spent those whole two or three weeks completely believing that they were monitoring everything I did. And the voice didn't stop either. I’d be back in the stockroom doing my pulls, feeling totally grounded, totally calm, and that guy's voice would still be right there behind my shoulder, laughing at me. Just chuckling away while I was trying to count inventory. 

So yeah, even when my mood was completely flat and normal for weeks, the tracking and the voice were still happening exactly the same way. It didn't let up for a single day, which is just... it's exhausting, you know? Because you think, 'Okay, I'm resting, I'm feeling fine, this should stop,' but it doesn't. It just keeps going.
Have you ever had any hallucinations or beliefs that people were tracking you only during times when your mood was high or irritable, and not when your mood was otherwise normal?

Well, no, not *only* then, because like I just spent all that time explaining to you, it definitely still happens when my mood is totally level and I'm resting. I know I just went on a whole tangent about that, but I just want to make sure we're on the same page, because that's the part that really proves to me how real this all is. It doesn't just go away when I calm down. 

But if you're asking if it *also* happens when I'm all revved up? Oh, absolutely. One hundred percent. It's almost like it gets mixed right in with all that crazy energy. Like, during those specific weeks I was telling you about, when I was barely sleeping at all and just running on pure adrenaline, I was talking absolutely nonstop about sneaker trends to anyone who would listen. The secondary market for sneakers was just blowing up and I knew exactly which drops were going to hit, and I was just feeling completely untouchable at work. Like nobody could even come close to my level. 

But even then, right in the middle of feeling like a total genius, I was still also convinced that the vendors were manipulating the numbers on me. I'd be looking at the invoices, talking a mile a minute to my supervisor about the sneaker shipments, and I could just see exactly where the suppliers were messing with the spreadsheets to sabotage my margins. And that voice I mentioned? The guy who laughs at me? He was there too, but instead of just chuckling while I was counting inventory, I sometimes heard that voice actively pushing me to move faster. It was like he was egging me on, rushing me to outsmart them before they ruined my buys. 

So it's not like the tracking or the voice takes a break when I'm in that unstoppable zone. They're right there with me. It's just that when I'm that energized, I feel like I'm racing against them, trying to beat the vendors at their own game while this voice is just constantly in my ear telling me to speed up. So, to answer your question, no, it's not *only* when I'm high or irritable, but it definitely, absolutely happens during those times too. It never really stops, no matter what my energy is doing.
During those times when your energy was very high, did you ever need to be hospitalized or have major trouble keeping up at work because of your behavior?

Well, no, I haven't been hospitalized or anything extreme like that. I haven't been locked up. But as for work... man, work has been a whole different story. My job has actually taken a real hit lately. 

It’s not that I couldn't keep up with the physical pace—like I said, I was moving a mile a minute—but my decision-making just went completely off the rails. Because I felt so untouchable and so sure of my own strategies, I was making these totally impulsive purchasing calls. I'd just lock in these massive bulk buys without running the numbers by anyone else because I just *knew* I was right about the market trends. But because my head was completely in the clouds with all these grand plans, I was actually dropping the ball on the basic stuff. I ended up completely missing my standard buying deadlines. The routine paperwork just slipped right by me. 

And then, of course, there’s the stuff with the vendors that I was telling you about earlier. I really damaged some important vendor relationships because I was just snapping at them, demanding things move at my speed. It got so bad that my supervisor actually pulled me into the office and gave me a formal warning. He sat me down with this whole written write-up about my erratic behavior and told me I was a liability, which... I mean, I was just trying to make the company money, but I guess I was too intense about it. 

And honestly, it’s not even just contained to the warehouse or the office. It bleeds into my personal life, too. I’ve completely pulled away from my friends. I used to be a pretty social guy, you know? We used to go to these local gallery nights downtown, just walking around, looking at art, hanging out. And I was part of this whole group that did volleyball weekends. Just normal, fun stuff. But I’ve completely stopped showing up for all of it. When I'm buzzing like that, or when I'm furious about getting a formal warning at work, I just don't have the patience to stand around a gallery making small talk or play a casual game of volleyball. Everyone else just feels too slow. So I just ghosted everybody. My whole routine is just totally shot. So, yeah, no hospital, but definitely major, major trouble keeping my life on track.
Have you ever had the voices or belief that people were tracking you when you were not having a manic or irritable episode?

Yeah, I mean, I feel like we're kind of circling back to what I was saying a few minutes ago, doc, but yes, absolutely. I want to be really clear about this because it's the part that messes with my head the most. 

Even during a calmer stretch, like that time I was telling you about when I was actually sleeping more normally and getting a full night's rest instead of pacing a hole in my floor... I wasn't keyed up at all. I wasn't irritable, I wasn't snapping at my supervisor, and I definitely wasn't feeling like I was running the whole market or single-handedly controlling the sneaker industry. I was just totally level. But even with all that calm, I still spent a few weeks completely believing that people were tracking my buys. 

I'd be sitting there, totally rested, just looking at my screen, and I'd know they were monitoring my purchase orders. And it wasn't just the tracking, either. I was still hearing the voice in the stockroom. I'd be back there pulling inventory, feeling completely normal, not a drop of that crazy adrenaline in my system, and that guy would still be right there, just laughing at me. 

It’s honestly exhausting to even try to make sense of it, because you’d think if you just get your sleep and your energy goes back to normal, your brain would give you a break, right? Like, if I'm not running around trying to dominate the secondary market, why am I still dealing with this? But it just doesn't matter. My mood can be totally fine, completely flat, not manic or whatever you want to call it, and the tracking and the voice just do not care. They just keep happening anyway. So, yeah, definitely.
When you are not having any manic or irritable episode, do the voices or the belief that people are tracking you still continue?

Uh, wait, didn't I... I feel like I literally just answered this exact thing, doc. Are you getting all this down? Because, yeah, like I was just saying a second ago, yes. It definitely continues. I'll explain it again if you need me to, because I really want to make sure you're understanding this part since it's what drives me the most crazy. 

Even during a much calmer stretch—and I'm talking about a period where I was actually sleeping more normally, going to bed at a reasonable time, getting a solid eight hours, waking up feeling totally rested. I wasn't keyed up, and I definitely wasn't feeling like I was running the whole market or single-handedly controlling the wholesale sneaker game. My brain just wasn't spinning like that. But even with all that peace and quiet in my mood, I still spent a few weeks completely believing that people were tracking my buys. I'd be sitting at my desk, totally relaxed, but I just knew they were watching my purchase orders and messing with things. 

And it was the exact same deal with the voice. I'd be back there in the stockroom, just casually counting shoeboxes, taking my time, no adrenaline at all, and I'd still be hearing that voice in the stockroom just mocking me. It went on for weeks like that while I was totally level. So, yeah, whether I'm bouncing off the walls or just completely chill, it doesn't matter. It still happens.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest or pleasure in things almost every day?

Well, depressed? I mean, I don't know if I'd call it depressed, exactly, but... yeah, there are definitely these long stretches, definitely more than two weeks, where I just completely bottom out. It's like all the air gets let out of the tire, you know? Like, when I'm up, I'm trying to buy out entire warehouses, and then suddenly... I just crash. And it's not just feeling sad, it's just this total, heavy emptiness. 

Like, on my off days during those times, I don't even leave my apartment. I just sit there on my couch, for hours and hours, just mindlessly scrolling through my phone. I'll be looking at all these new sneaker drops—which usually I'd be obsessed with, right? I'd be analyzing the resale value, planning my moves. But during these crashes, I'm just scrolling and I don't even care. It's just colors on a screen. I feel absolutely nothing about it. 

And my friends... man, I was telling you earlier about the volleyball weekends and the gallery nights downtown, right? Well, during these slumps, my phone will be buzzing with texts from them, asking where I am, trying to get me to come out and play a few games or just grab a drink, and I just stare at the screen. I just dodge all of it. I don't answer a single text. It honestly just feels like way too much physical and mental work to even type back "I can't make it." Just the thought of trying to form a sentence and send it feels like trying to lift a boulder. So I just sit there in the quiet, scrolling, not caring about anything, ignoring everyone. It just feels like my whole brain shuts off and I can't find the switch to turn it back on. So, yeah, I definitely have those periods where everything just feels totally pointless and flat.
When you hear the voice, does it ever comment on or reflect your mood—like during high-energy times it boosts you, and during low times it becomes critical or mocking?

Well, as far as matching my mood... it's not really like it changes its tune depending on how I'm feeling, you know? It's more like... well, let me just tell you exactly how it happens, because it's so specific. It's always this same man's voice. And it doesn't really matter if I'm flying high and energized or totally crashed out and empty, it's just... there. 

Like, a lot of times I'll be at work, right? I'll be in the back in the stockroom, just doing my normal inventory stuff, breaking down boxes, checking the SKUs on the new shipments. And suddenly, clear as day, I'll hear this guy's voice like it's coming from right behind my shoulder. And he'll just say, "Move faster, Scott." Just like that. It sounds so incredibly real, doc. 

Or the other time it happens a lot is when I'm in my car. I'll be driving back from a vendor meeting—like, maybe I just spent two hours negotiating a bulk buy on some high-demand sneakers, trying to secure the best wholesale price so I can flip them. I'm cruising down the highway, totally alone in the car, windows up, radio maybe on low, and I'll hear him right from the backseat, just laughing. Literally laughing at my picks! Like he's mocking the deals I just made, acting like I bought a bunch of garbage that won't ever sell. 

And every single time it happens, whether I'm deep in the stockroom or doing sixty on the highway, I whip my head around. I mean, I've almost swerved my car before because it startles me so bad. I turn around, fully expecting to see some guy standing right there in my personal space, breathing down my neck, and... nobody's there. It's just empty air. Just my empty backseat or a wall of shoeboxes. 

So, yeah, I wouldn't say he ever boosts me up or acts like a cheerleader when I'm manic or anything like that. He's just always there, telling me to hurry up or laughing at my business choices, no matter what kind of mood I'm in. It's incredibly frustrating, honestly, because I'll be trying to run the profit margins in my head on the drive back, trying to focus on my job, and I just get completely derailed by this guy who isn't even physically in the room with me.
During those times when your mood and energy are very high, do you feel like you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Oh, absolutely. It’s actually crazy how little sleep I need when I get like that. I mean, there have been plenty of weeks—entire stretches, really—where I sleep maybe three or four hours a night, tops. And it's not like I'm tossing and turning, miserable, trying to sleep and failing. It's more like... I'll finally force myself into bed at maybe 3 AM after scouring the overseas markets for new drops, right? Because the international markets operate on totally different time zones, and you gotta be on top of that if you want to secure the rare colorways before the other buyers swoop in. 

So I'll lay down, get my three or four hours, and then boom. My eyes just snap open. Usually way before my alarm even has a chance to go off. And I don't feel groggy at all, not even a little bit. I wake up feeling completely wired and ready. Like, totally rested, as if I just slept for a full ten hours. My heart is already pumping, my brain is already calculating wholesale profit margins, and I just start thinking that lying in bed is just wasting time I could use to make moves. You know? 

Like, I'll literally be lying there thinking, why am I just horizontal in the dark when there's money to be made and inventory to secure? Every single minute I spend with my eyes closed is a minute somebody else is out there buying up the stock I need to be flipping. So I just jump right out of bed, boot up my laptop, and get right back to it. I don't even need a cup of coffee on those days. I just run on this pure, buzzing energy for weeks at a time, and three hours of sleep feels like more than enough to keep me operating at maximum capacity.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks when the voices and beliefs were still there, but you were not having any mood episode at all?

Yeah, actually, I know exactly what you mean, because I can think of a really specific time that happened. It was, I don't know, maybe a couple of months ago? I was having this really... I guess you'd call it a calmer stretch. 

Like, I wasn't crashing. I wasn't sitting on the couch ignoring my friends and feeling totally dead inside like I told you about before. But I also wasn't wired at all. I wasn't feeling like I was running the whole market or trying to buy out every warehouse in Europe. I was just... regular. Normal. I was actually getting a solid seven or eight hours of sleep a night, which is crazy for me. I'd go to bed at like midnight, wake up at 8 AM, and I'd actually make breakfast. Usually, I skip breakfast when I'm on my grind because I don't have time, but I was actually making eggs and toast, taking a shower, just going to work and doing my shifts at a totally average, boring pace. 

But the crazy part is, even though my mood was totally leveled out and I was sleeping normally... that other stuff didn't stop. Like, I still spent a solid two, maybe three weeks during that exact same calm period completely convinced that other people were tracking my buys. 

I'd be looking at my wholesale accounts, just doing standard restocking for the store, and I just *knew* that some of the rival buyers had tapped into my IP address or had some kind of algorithm watching my purchase history so they could snipe my deals. I got so paranoid about it that I started using a VPN and driving to different coffee shops miles away just to place a basic order for, like, standard white Air Force 1s. Which is honestly ridiculous when you think about it, because nobody needs to steal a strategy for basic white AF1s, they're literally the most basic shoe! But I was just so sure my moves were being monitored. 

And the voice was still there, too. That same guy. I'd be in the stockroom at work, totally well-rested, no crazy buzzing energy, just breaking down cardboard boxes at a normal, steady pace, and I'd still hear him right over my shoulder going, "Move faster, Scott." Or he'd be laughing at me from the backseat while I was driving home, even though I hadn't even made any big, risky wholesale moves that day for him to laugh at! 

So, yeah, I'd say for at least a few weeks there, I was completely baseline with my energy and my mood, just living a totally average routine... but I was still dealing with the tracking stuff and hearing that guy in the stockroom the whole time. It really doesn't seem to care if I'm hyped up or not, it just kind of does its own thing.
Have you ever had any periods when you were completely free of the voices and the tracking belief?

Well, free of them? No, not really. Not anytime recently, anyway. I mean, if I really sit back and think about it, trying to pinpoint exactly when my head was totally clear of all that... it's been a long time. I'd say the suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now, pretty much non-stop. 

I remember specifically because it was right around the time the holiday sneaker drops started getting leaked last year, and I was trying to get ahead of the Q4 rush. You know how crazy the fourth quarter is in retail, right? It's absolute madness. Everyone is trying to source inventory, the supply chains get all jammed up, and that's when I first started noticing the guy's voice in the stockroom. It was also exactly when I started getting that creeping feeling that my IP was being monitored by the other buyers who were trying to snipe my wholesale pallets. 

And since then? Since that whole holiday prep period ten months ago? No breaks. Not a single one. Even when I went on a little weekend trip to my buddy's place upstate back in the spring, thinking maybe I just needed to step away from the screens and the inventory lists for a minute... nope. Still there. I was still hearing the voice in the passenger seat on the drive up, and I was still wondering if my phone was pinging my search history to competitors while we were just sitting around a fire pit. 

So yeah, for about ten months straight, it's just been my reality, day in and day out. I just haven't had a single stretch where it all went away, no matter if I'm working, sleeping, manic, or totally calm. It's just always going.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when the voices or tracking beliefs were present while your mood was not high, irritable, or depressed at all?

Yeah, exactly, I think that's what I was just trying to say a minute ago! Like, it's exactly like that. Even during that calmer stretch I was just talking about, you know? The one where I was sleeping way more normally, getting my full eight hours, and definitely not feeling like I was running the whole market or anything crazy like that... I still spent a few weeks right then believing people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing the voice in the stockroom, too. 

It’s just wild to think about because, like, you’d think if I wasn't hyped up or irritable or feeling super down, that all the other stuff would just fade out with it, right? Like, if my mood is totally fine and boring, my brain should be boring too. But nope. I'd be standing there, completely chilled out, totally normal energy, just folding a stack of hoodies or organizing the back room without rushing at all, and I'd still be looking over my shoulder wondering who was watching my inventory screens. Or I'd hear that guy making comments while I was just doing totally mundane stuff. 

So yeah, definitely, to answer your question. A solid two or three weeks of just... totally normal, flat mood, not high or depressed at all, but all the tracking beliefs and the voices were still fully there, 100 percent. It just didn't seem to matter that my mood was completely fine.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing people were tracking you, but you were not having any manic, irritable, or depressed episode at all?

Wait, I feel like we're going in circles here, doc, did you just ask me that again? Or is there like a subtle difference in the medical words you're using this time? Because yeah, like I was literally just saying a second ago, it’s exactly like that. I'll explain it again though, because it's honestly the weirdest part of all this to try and wrap my head around. 

Even during that calmer stretch I was telling you about—the one where I was actually sleeping more normally, getting a solid eight hours instead of just staring at my inventory screens till 4 AM, and definitely not feeling like I was running the whole market or controlling the entire sneaker resale ecosystem... I still spent a few weeks right then believing people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing the voice in the stockroom, too. 

Like, I’d be in the back room at the shop, just breaking down the big brown shipping boxes—you know, the bulk ones that hold like twelve pairs of shoes at a time—and my mood would be completely flat. Not manic, not depressed, not snappy or irritable with my coworkers. Just totally average, doing a boring task. But I'm still constantly checking the VPN on my phone because I'm completely convinced rival buyers are mirroring my IP address to steal my wholesale strategy, and I'm still hearing that guy's voice right over my shoulder telling me to move faster while I'm just trying to flatten cardboard. 

It’s like my mood took a vacation and just leveled out completely, but the tracking stuff and the voice just stayed clocked in for overtime, you know what I mean? So, yeah, definitely a solid few weeks of exactly what you're asking about, 100 percent.
Have the voices or tracking beliefs ever continued for at least two weeks when your mood was not high, irritable, or depressed?

Okay, seriously doc, are you messing with me right now? Or is this like a psychological memory test or something? Because I swear on my life, this is the third time you've asked me the exact same question, just shuffling the words around a little bit. 

I don't know how many different ways I can explain this specific timeline to you, but yes. Yes, they continued. Like I was just saying, I literally just laid it all out for you twice. There was that calmer stretch I had. My mood was totally fine. I wasn't hyped up, I wasn't irritable, I wasn't depressed at all. I was actually sleeping so normally, like getting a full, solid eight hours, waking up feeling rested instead of jolting awake at 3 AM to check the Asian wholesale markets.
